entries.title: Proverbs 27:3
segments:
3. heavy--The literal sense of "heavy," applied to material subjects, illustrates its figurative, "grievous," applied to moral. 
 
    a fool's wrath--is unreasonable and excessive.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:4
segments: 4. envy--or, "jealousy" (compare Margin;
), is more unappeasable than the simpler bad passions.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:5
segments: 5, 6. secret love--not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:7
segments: 7. The luxury of wealth confers less happiness than the healthy appetite of labor.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:8
segments: 8. Such are not only out of place, but out of duty and in danger.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:9
segments:
9. rejoice the heart--the organ of perceiving what pleases the senses. 
 
    sweetness ... counsel--or, "wise counsel is also pleasing."

entries.title: Proverbs 27:10
segments: 10. Adhere to tried friends. The ties of blood may be less reliable than those of genuine friendship.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:11
segments: 11. The wisdom of children both reflects credit on parents and contributes to their aid in difficulties.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:16
segments:
16. hideth--or, "restrains" (that is, tries to do it); is as fruitless an effort, as that of holding the wind. 
 
    the ointment of his right hand--the organ of power (
). His right hand endeavors to repress perfume, but vainly. Some prefer: "His right hand comes on oil," that is, "cannot take hold." Such a woman cannot be tamed.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:17
segments: 17. a man sharpeneth ... friend--that is, conversation promotes intelligence, which the face exhibits.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:18
segments: 18. Diligence secures a reward, even for the humble servant.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:19
segments: 19. We may see our characters in the developed tempers of others.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:20
segments: 20. Men's cupidity is as insatiable as the grave.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:21
segments:
21. Praise tests character. 
 
    a man to his praise--according to his praise, as he bears it. Thus vain men seek it, weak men are inflated by it, wise men disregard it, &c.

entries.title: Proverbs 27:22
segments: 22. The obstinate wickedness of such is incurable by the heaviest inflictions.
